[Thinking]
Okay, let's tackle this question: "Kuka oli Venäjän viimeinen tsaari ennen Venäjän vallankumousta?" which translates to "Who was the last Tsar of Russia before the Russian Revolution?" 

First, I need to recall the key historical facts. The Russian Revolution happened in 1917, which led to the end of the Romanov dynasty. The last Tsar would be the one who was overthrown during that revolution. I remember that Nicholas II was the Tsar during World War I and was forced to abdicate in 1917. But wait, let me make sure. There was also his father, Alexander III, but he died earlier, in 1894. So Nicholas II succeeded him. 

Wait, the question specifies "ennen Venäjän vallankumousta" which is "before the Russian Revolution". The revolution happened in 1917, so the last Tsar before that would be the one who was in power right up until the revolution. Nicholas II abdicated in March 1917 (February in the Julian calendar, which Russia used at the time), so he was the last Tsar. After his abdication, there was a provisional government, and then the Bolsheviks took over later that year. 

But I should check if there's any confusion with other revolutions. There was the 1905 revolution, but that wasn't the one that ended the monarchy. The main revolution that ended the Tsarist regime was the February Revolution of 1917, which forced Nicholas II to abdicate. So he is definitely the last Tsar. 

Also, his full name is Nikolai Aleksandrovich Romanov. Sometimes spelled Nicholas II in English. In Finnish, it's probably "Nikolai II" or "Nikolai Aleksandrovitš Romanov". The question is in Finnish, so the answer should use the Finnish naming convention. 

Wait, let me confirm the Finnish spelling. In Finnish sources, he is commonly referred to as "Nikolai II" or "Viimeinen tsaari Nikolai II". Also, his family was executed in 1918 by the Bolsheviks. 

Is there any chance someone might confuse him with Michael Alexandrovich? Because after Nicholas abdicated, he initially named his brother Michael as successor, but Michael refused the throne the next day, which effectively ended the Romanov dynasty. So technically, Michael was never really the Tsar, as he didn't accept the position. Therefore, Nicholas II remains the last reigning Tsar. 

So the answer should be Nicholas II (Nikolai II in Finnish). Let me check Finnish Wikipedia to confirm. According to Finnish sources, "Venäjän viimeinen tsaari oli Nikolai II, joka luopui kruunusta helmikuun vallankumouksen seurauksena vuonna 1917." Yes, that's correct. 

Also, the user might be thinking of the October Revolution, but the abdication happened during the February Revolution. The October Revolution was when the Bolsheviks took power from the provisional government. So the last Tsar was indeed Nicholas II. 

No other contenders. Alexander III died in 1894, so he wasn't the last. Nicholas II reigned from 1894 until 1917. Therefore, the answer is clear.
[/Thinking]

Venäjän viimeinen tsaari ennen Venäjän vallankumousta oli **Nikolai II** (täysin Nikolai Aleksandrovitš Romanov). Hän nousi valtaan vuonna 1894 isänsä Aleksanteri III:n kuoltua ja luopui kruunusta helmikuun vallankumouksen (maaliskuussa 1917 nykyisen kalenterin mukaan) seurauksena. Vaikka hän nimitti aluksi veljensä Mihail Aleksandrovitšin seuraajakseen, tämä kieltäytyi kruunusta seuraavana päivänä, mikä merkitsi Romanov-suvun hallinnon loppua. Nikolai II ja hänen perheensä teloitettiin bolševikkien toimesta vuonna 1918 Jekaterinburgissa. Häntä pidetään laajasti Venäjän historian viimeisenä tsaarina.
